extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of social science/political economy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for conducting and evaluating sociological inquiry and related abstract sciences (e.g., political economy), emphasizing appropriate deductive methods, verification, limits of prediction, and the creation of disciplinary sub-branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete Deductive Method (consider multiple causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Social Science... is a deductive science; not, indeed, after the model of geometry, but after that of the more complex physical sciences. It infers the law of each effect from the laws of causation on which that effect depends; not, however, from the law merely of one cause, as in the geometrical method, but by considering all the causes which conjunctly influence the effect, and compounding their laws with one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat social effects as aggregate results of many causes. Use the model of complex physical sciences (e.g., astronomy) rather than geometric single-cause reasoning. Expect need for adaptations and precautions because of increased complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification (empirical collation of deductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: This remedy consists in the process which, under the name of Verification, we have characterized as the third essential constituent part of the Deductive Method; that of collating the conclusions of the ratiocination either with the concrete phenomena themselves, or, when such are obtainable, with their empirical laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deduction alone is insufficient — reliable sociological inference depends on agreement between a priori reasoning and a posteriori observation. In complex cases verification may precede or invert the order of deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit conclusions to tendencies, not precise predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sociology, considered as a system of deductions a priori, can not be a science of positive predictions, but only of tendencies. We may be able to conclude... that a particular cause will operate in a certain manner unless counteracted; but we can never be assured to what extent or amount it will so operate, or affirm with certainty that it will not be counteracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use knowledge of tendencies for guidance and risk management rather than infallible forecasting. Prepare for counteracting influences and partial outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General propositions are hypothetical and context-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: All the general propositions which can be framed by the deductive science, are therefore, in the strictest sense of the word, hypothetical. They are grounded on some suppositious set of circumstances, and declare how some given cause would operate in those circumstances, supposing that no others were combined with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying general theorems, explicitly state the assumed circumstances; revise premises when applying to different societies or historical periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Intermixture of Laws (consensus across social phenomena)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mode of production of all social phenomena is one great case of Intermixture of Laws. Whatever affects, in an appreciable degree, any one element of the social state, affects through it all the other elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not isolate social variables without considering their pervasive interconnections; recognize systemic feedbacks and cross-influences when analyzing any phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt general theorems to particular societies
rubrics_metrics.description: The deductive science of society will not lay down a theorem, asserting in a universal manner the effect of any cause; but will rather teach us how to frame the proper theorem for the circumstances of any given case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each application, reconstruct the set of influencing circumstances and perform the analysis anew rather than mechanically transferring results across dissimilar contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit complexity of hypothetical combinations to preserve value
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering... how accelerating a ratio the uncertainty of our conclusions increases as we attempt to take the effect of a greater number of concurrent causes into our calculations, the hypothetical combinations of circumstances on which we construct the general theorems of the science, can not be made very complex, without so rapidly accumulating a liability to error as must soon deprive our conclusions of all value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance inclusiveness with tractability: keep hypothetical models limited enough to retain informative value, and increase individualizing detail only as feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate branches where one class of causes predominates
rubrics_metrics.description: Different species of social facts are in the main dependent, immediately and in the first resort, on different kinds of causes; and therefore not only may with advantage, but must, be studied apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create disciplinary sub-branches (e.g., political economy) to study phenomena primarily driven by a particular class of causes, while remembering their secondary interdependence with the rest of the social system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Economy's methodological abstraction (treat desire for wealth as sole end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Political Economy... concerns itself only with 'such of the phenomena of the social state as take place in consequence of the pursuit of wealth. It makes entire abstraction of every other human passion or motive; except those which may be regarded as perpetually antagonizing principles to the desire of wealth, namely, aversion to labor, and desire of the present enjoyment of costly indulgences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the simplification of treating pursuit of wealth as the dominant motive to derive core laws (e.g., of rent, profits, wages), then correct conclusions by accounting for other motives when applying to real societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study causes one at a time then compound
rubrics_metrics.description: When an effect depends on a concurrence of causes, these causes must be studied one at a time, and their laws separately investigated, if we wish, through the causes, to obtain the power of either predicting or controlling the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive the law of the effect by composing the separately understood laws of the contributing causes; analogous to solving component forces in physics before combining them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious applying locally-drawn abstractions to other societies
rubrics_metrics.description: Though many of its conclusions are only locally true, its method of investigation is applicable universally; and as whoever has solved a certain number of algebraic equations, can without difficulty solve all others of the same kind, so whoever knows the political economy of England... knows that of all nations, actual or possible, provided he have good sense enough not to expect the same conclusion to issue from varying premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transferring theories developed for one society (e.g., England under free competition) to another, trace back the demonstrations and introduce new premises appropriate to the target society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility may justify departing from strict scientific arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only in a few of the most striking cases... are these corrections interpolated into the expositions of political economy itself; the strictness of purely scientific arrangement being thereby somewhat departed from, for the sake of practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit selective incorporation of empirical corrections into abstract theory when doing so materially improves practical relevance, while noting the departure from theoretical purity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inverse (inductive) and direct deduction flexibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of deducing our conclusions by reasoning, and verifying them by observation, we in some cases begin by obtaining them provisionally from specific experience, and afterward connect them with the principles of human nature by a priori reasonings, which reasonings are thus a real Verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ both orders: derive provisional laws from observation where deduction is inapplicable, then integrate them into broader a priori frameworks; both directions are legitimate depending on complexity and available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Ethology: study causes of national/collective character
rubrics_metrics.description: I allude to what may be termed Political Ethology, or the theory of the causes which determine the type of character belonging to a people or to an age... the laws of national (or collective) character are by far the most important class of sociological laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize inquiry into how institutions and social arrangements shape national character, because character both results from and strongly conditions other social phenomena; acknowledge infancy of ethology and attendant uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits of human faculties in compounding many tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the resources of science are not sufficient to enable us to calculate, a priori, with complete precision, the mutual action of three bodies gravitating toward one another, it may be judged with what prospect of success we should endeavor to calculate the result of the conflicting tendencies which are acting in a thousand different directions...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge practical limits to exact a priori calculation in complex social systems; rely on distinguishing tendencies and relative strengths rather than exact quantitative aggregation.
